hero.title: Venerdì
hero.lead: You land in the morning, Laurin and Olivia land at night. This is the bit in between.

arrival.title: From the airport
arrival.lead: If you're on the 06:00 Ryanair (FR134), you land at Fiumicino at 08:10. It's the only direct morning flight from Berlin, and lately it's been landing early. From Termini, bus 40 or 64 to Argentina is about 20 min. Drop your bag off first, I'll be at breakfast from 09:45, no rush.

options.detail: 32 min non-stop, every 15 min, €14. Tap your card or phone at the platform gate, no ticket needed.
€8, every 15 min. It skips Termini and stops at Trastevere and Ostiense instead.
€55 to anywhere inside the old walls. Say 'tariffa fissa' before you get in, and ignore anyone offering a ride inside the terminal.

arrival.warning: No strikes listed for Ryanair or Rome transport on Friday (checked 8 Oct).

stops.title: Maritozzo, standing up
stops.body: Basically a soft bun with way too much whipped cream in it. They fill it when you order.
stops.move: Order 'un maritozzo e un cappuccino al banco'. Al banco just means at the counter, and it's about half the price of sitting down.

swaps.title: Coming through Termini?
swaps.body: Regoli is 8 minutes from the station and does the other famous maritozzo. Open from 06:30.

stops.title: Second breakfast
stops.body: Old-school Jewish bakery. No sign, not much smiling, and the cakes look burnt on purpose. The ricotta and sour cherry tart is the one, and it's not too sweet.
stops.move: Cash, and know what you want before the counter. The tart tends to sell out before noon.

stops.title: Caesar was stabbed here. Now it's cats.
stops.body: You see all of it from the railing, for free.
stops.move: The cat sanctuary only lets people in from noon.

stops.title: The dome that isn't there
stops.body: Not a church visit, promise. They ran out of money for a real dome, so in 1685 a painter faked one on a flat ceiling. Stand on the little marble disc in the middle and it looks 3D. Keep walking and it falls apart.

stops.title: Coffee, round two
stops.body: Get the gran caffè. It comes already sweetened, with a thick foam on top. Pay at the till first, then hand the receipt over.
stops.move: Say 'amaro' and they leave the sugar out.

stops.title: Look up
stops.body: A 2,000-year-old concrete dome with a hole in the roof. Stand right under the hole. If it rains, it rains inside.
stops.move: I'm booking the 11:00–12:00 slot for both of us. The tickets have our names on them, so bring ID.

stops.title: Just passing through
stops.body: It sits on top of a Roman stadium, that's why it's so long. We walk it end to end, don't eat here, then take bus 30 south.

transferToNext.note: Bus 30 (every 10 min) from the Rinascimento stop, direction Laurentina: 12 min to Marmorata/Vanvitelli, then 8 min on foot. Taxi about €12–15.

stops.title: Lunch at the market
stops.body: Testaccio's covered market. The stall we want is Mordi e Vai: slow-cooked beef in a roll dipped in its own broth. Then we split a trapizzino from the shop around the corner that invented them.
stops.move: Bring cash and don't wear white. The good stalls sell out by about 13:30.

swaps.title: If we stay central
swaps.body: Supplì at Supplizio, then pizza bianca by the slice from Roscioli's bakery. Both five minutes from Navona.

swaps.title: Pastry number three
swaps.body: On Via Marmorata, on the way from the market to the cemetery. Cornetti, or a few mignon (tiny pastries).

stops.title: A pyramid and a poet
stops.body: Rome has a pyramid, a tomb from 12 BC, and behind it a really quiet garden. Keats is buried here under a stone that doesn't even have his name on it.
stops.move: They ask for €5 each at the gate. A couple of photos is fine, just not for Instagram.

rain.title: Statues in a power plant
rain.body: Marble gods and emperors standing next to giant diesel engines in an old power station. Weird mix, and usually pretty empty.
rain.move: Go straight to the engine hall.

transferIn.note: Walk 10 minutes to Piramide, one stop to Garbatella, then 7 minutes on foot.

stops.title: Pick up the bibs
stops.body: Startnummern (start numbers) for Sunday :) The race village is right next to Eataly, so snacks are sorted too.
stops.move: We each need our printed confirmation letter and ID, and the wave time is on the letter. From Piramide, take the underpass towards Eataly instead of crossing the big square.

transferToNext.note: The Aventine is the day's only real hill. A taxi up is about €10. Walking it is 1.9 km and 25 minutes: flat until the last stretch, then 30 m up Via di Porta Lavernale.

stops.title: Look through the keyhole
stops.body: A green door with a queue in front of it. Through the keyhole: a hedge tunnel, and St Peter's dome at the end of it. Then Santa Sabina next door, where a little window in the porch shows an orange tree that's supposedly 800 years old.
stops.move: If the queue is huge, we do Santa Sabina first and come back.

stops.title: The orange garden
stops.body: Free view over the whole city. The gates close at 18:00, so around 17:10 we take the old cobbled lane down at the back.

rain.title: A corridor that lies
rain.body: A colonnade that looks like a long gallery with a life-size statue at the end. It's under 9 metres deep and the statue is tiny. Roscioli's bakery is round the corner if we need pizza bianca.
rain.move: Last access to the colonnade is 18:30.

transferIn.note: From the keyhole, about €10. Skip the Orange Garden in the rain.

stops.title: The medieval lie detector
stops.body: A giant stone face that supposedly bites liars. Worth it if the queue is short. If not, we wave through the gate and move on.

stops.title: Sunset from the typewriter
stops.body: Romans call this giant white monument 'the typewriter' and mostly complain about it. But a glass lift goes to the roof, and the view up there is huge. Sunset is 18:29.
stops.move: We need to be inside by 18:45. Stairs up to the first terrace, then the lift does the rest.

swaps.title: If we skip the ticket
swaps.body: The Capitoline museums' café terrace, a few minutes away, looks west over the domes. Part of it has a roof.

rain.title: Kandinsky instead
rain.body: A big Kandinsky show right on Piazza Venezia, open until 21:00 on Fridays. Mostly colour and shapes.

stops.title: Carbs, early
stops.body: Loud, packed pizzeria right behind the Colosseum, so we walk past it on the way. Really thin pizza, and supplì: pull one apart and the cheese stretches like a phone cord.
stops.move: I'll book 19:30. They only take bookings a week ahead, so the form goes in on Friday 9 October.

swaps.title: If Li Rioni is full
swaps.body: Big, noisy pizzeria in Monti, 9 minutes from the Vittoriano, good fried starters. Phone bookings only.

swaps.title: If we'd rather have pasta
swaps.body: Small family trattoria in Monti, all the Roman pastas for about €14. Dinner starts at 19:30, phone to book.

stops.title: That's Friday
stops.body: Laurin and Olivia land around nine, and by then the day is done. Saturday is for doing nothing :)

book.label: Pantheon tickets
book.detail: Named, 11:00–12:00 slot. I need your full name as it is on your ID.

book.label: Vittoriano rooftop
book.detail: Dated ticket, no time slot. €18, or €5 if EU and 18–24.

book.label: Li Rioni, 19:30
book.detail: Booking form opens Friday 9 Oct. I'll call after 19:00 that day to make sure.

book.label: Race confirmation letters
book.detail: Download, print, check for the two green OKs and the wave time.

practical.title: ID
practical.body: The Pantheon checks names, and the race checks everything.

practical.title: Your race letter, printed
practical.body: We each need our own to get the bibs.

practical.title: A light layer
practical.body: Some churches want shoulders covered, and evenings get cool.

practical.title: A water bottle
practical.body: The little iron fountains everywhere (nasoni) are drinking water. Block the spout with a finger and it shoots up.

practical.title: Your card or phone
practical.body: Buses take contactless: tap once per ride, €1.50. Phone in the front pocket around Termini.

practical.title: Comfy shoes
practical.body: About 8 km, a lot of it cobbles.

budgetNote: EU and 18–24? The Pantheon drops to €2 and the Vittoriano to €5.

footer.line: Hours and prices checked on 8 October.

paras: You were here three years ago. I was here as a kid and remember basically nothing. So I skipped most of the big stuff and went for things you probably didn't do last time: a fake dome, a pyramid, a keyhole, and a lot of pastries.
Sunday is our first Halbmarathon (half marathon), so legs come first. About 8 km of walking all day, a taxi up the one real hill, and dinner early.
Everything outdoors has a backup if it rains. I'm sorting the tickets, you just bring ID :)
